# What vim does to a window's scroll position, measured 2026-09-04 against
# /opt/homebrew/bin/vim, VIM 9.2 patches 1-321, through
#
#   vim --clean -i NONE --not-a-term -S probe.vim -s KEYS f.txt
#
# over a file of the lines "1" to "400". The window height is set with
# ":set lines=", the starting scroll position with winrestview(), and the
# answer read back with line('w0'), line('.') and &scroll through writefile(),
# which is the only way to ask a headless vim what it is showing.
#
# The columns are
#
#   keys  height  scrolloff  topline  cursor  ->  topline  cursor  scroll
#
# where the first topline and cursor are what vim reported BEFORE the keys and
# not what winrestview() was handed: a redraw normalises a position that
# violates 'scrolloff', so "topline 376 cursor 380" at 'scrolloff' 5 is really
# topline 375 by the time the key arrives, and a table that recorded the ask
# rather than the answer would be testing the harness.
#
# internal/window/scroll_test.go replays every row. A row that fails is vim
# disagreeing with this package, which is the only kind of failure this file
# can produce.

# Added 2026-09-05, same method and same file of the lines "1" to "400".
#
# The z family near the end of the buffer, where the bottom 'scrolloff' push
# has to stop once the last line is on the bottom row: at 'scrolloff' 3 every
# cursor from 397 to 400 gives the same top line, and at 0 they walk.
397Gzb        23  0    1    1 ->  375  397  11
398Gzb        23  0    1    1 ->  376  398  11
400Gzb        23  0    1    1 ->  378  400  11
397Gzb        23  3    1    1 ->  378  397  11
398Gzb        23  3    1    1 ->  378  398  11
399Gzb        23  3    1    1 ->  378  399  11
400Gzb        23  3    1    1 ->  378  400  11
398Gz-        23  3    1    1 ->  378  398  11
397Gzb        23  5    1    1 ->  378  397  11
400Gzb        23  5    1    1 ->  378  400  11

# CTRL-D with the window already past the last screenful, which zt, zz and
# CTRL-E can leave it. Vim's halfpage() walks the top forward one line at a
# time while w_botline is still inside the buffer, so it never moves the top
# BACKWARDS; the cursor moves the full 'scroll' either way.
Gzt<C-D>      23  0    1    1 ->  400  400  11
Gzt<C-D>      23  3    1    1 ->  397  400  11
Gzt<C-D>      23  5    1    1 ->  395  400  11
380Gzt<C-D>   23  0    1    1 ->  380  391  11
380Gzt<C-D>   23  3    1    1 ->  378  391  11
380Gzt<C-D>   23  5    1    1 ->  378  391  11
Gzz<C-D>      23  0    1    1 ->  389  400  11
Gzz<C-D>      23  3    1    1 ->  389  400  11

# CTRL-B from the same kind of window. The line that lands on the bottom row
# is the one below the old top, and it may not be the last line of the file,
# so a window showing one buffer line above a screen of tildes jumps further
# than the window less two. A count is worked out once and applied count
# times rather than being a repeat of the command.
Gzt<C-B>      23  0    1    1 ->  377  399  11
Gzt<C-B>      23  3    1    1 ->  376  395  11
Gzt<C-B>      23  5    1    1 ->  374  391  11
Gzb<C-B>      23  0    1    1 ->  357  379  11
Gzb<C-B>      23  3    1    1 ->  357  376  11
Gzb<C-B>      23  5    1    1 ->  357  374  11
400Gzt2<C-B>  23  0    1    1 ->  354  376  11
400Gzt2<C-B>  23  3    1    1 ->  355  374  11
400Gzt2<C-B>  23  5    1    1 ->  353  370  11

# A count on z+ and z^ is a line number, not a repeat: "[count]z+" is
# "[count]z<CR>", and "[count]z^" scrolls line [count] to the bottom and then
# does the bare z^ on the window that leaves.
2z+           23  0  100  110 ->    2    2  11
50z+          23  0  100  110 ->   50   50  11
100z+         23  0  100  110 ->  100  100  11
2z^           23  0  100  110 ->    1    1  11
50z^          23  0  100  110 ->    6   28  11
100z^         23  0  100  110 ->   56   78  11
2z+           23  3  100  110 ->    1    2  11
50z+          23  3  100  110 ->   47   50  11
100z+         23  3  100  110 ->   97  100  11
2z^           23  3  100  110 ->    1    1  11
50z^          23  3  100  110 ->   12   31  11
100z^         23  3  100  110 ->   62   81  11
50z+          23  5  100  110 ->   45   50  11
100z+         23  5  100  110 ->   95  100  11
50z^          23  5  100  110 ->   16   33  11
100z^         23  5  100  110 ->   66   83  11
